turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training data shows the highest reproducible efficiencies come from:
- n-i-p **FAMAPbI / FAMAPbBrI** absorbers with **SnO₂ or TiO₂** electron contacts and **Spiro-MeOTAD** hole contacts, especially with additional interfacial/contact modifiers and multi-step spin-coating.
- p-i-n **CsFAMAPbBrI** devices with **C60/PCBM/BCP** electron stacks and **PTAA** hole layers, with Ag or Cu contacts.

Evaluating the pool candidates against these high-efficiency analogues, the likely highest performers are:

- **c092**: FAMAPbI n-i-p on ITO/SnO₂-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO₃|Ag, spin>>spin — closely matches training cells near 20.2–20.4%.
- **c093**: CsFAMAPbBrI p-i-n with PCBM-60|BCP/PTAA/Ag — matches the 20.1–20.3% inverted PTAA class.
- **c085**: CsFAMAPbBrI p-i-n with C60|BCP/PTAA|PFN-Br/Cu — very close to the 20.1% C60/BCP/PTAA/Cu training recipe, with a beneficial PFN-Br contact.
- **c008**: FAMAPbI n-i-p with SnO₂-c/Spiro-MeOTAD/Au and double spin-coating — standard high-efficiency n-i-p stack.
- **c099**: FAMAPbBrI n-i-p on TiO₂-mp with Au-nanowire|Spiro-MeOTAD — high-efficiency base stack with likely plasmonic/conductivity enhancement.

Final: c092, c093, c085, c008, c099
